title: Perf run 20261016-0821
heading: No speed change this run: dead CSS removed, five checks that could not fail now can, and a replay failure that says why, once
meta: This run made the game no faster and no slower. Against main b455e10, the final code (measured on 3b73fe5; the one code commit after it, fc71549, changes only what happens when a replay fails) has no headline row called better or worse in 4 pairs, and memory is unchanged. The PR removes 47 lines of the app's CSS that never applied, adds a console warning (said once per game) when a game's record can't be replayed, and makes five tests and lint rules able to fail on the faults they name. The shared game's first screen leans slower in the bench since the labels started being centred by their capital letters (#155), but no comparison calls it, and the same code compared with itself leans as far. It stays in the ledger as a question about the bench, not a decision for you.

needs.intro: Nothing waits on you. The skill asks me to list every headline row that is more than 3% slower at the median pair, or slower in every pair, even when the comparison does not call it. None of these is called, the branch changes no code these rows run, and the same code compared with itself leans as far on the rows that comparison covered.

  • 8 pairs (ab-20261016-0821-final8.md): the joiner's picture 1.25 1.08 1.04 0.88 1.01 1.20 0.94 1.18 (median 1.06); reopening 1.14 0.91 1.23 0.87 0.96 2.24 0.97 1.72 (1.06); the opponent's move 1.07 1.05 1.09 1.13 1.11 0.80 1.39 0.74 (1.08). The player's move settled at 0.96.
  • The same code against itself, 8 pairs (ab-20261016-0821-aa-final.md): the joiner's picture median 1.06 (6 of 8 pairs slower), the shared game's page 1.105 (7 of 8), reopening 0.97. The move rows had no such comparison this run.

The last code commit, fc71549, changes only what happens when a replay fails, which no bench row runs, so these figures stand for it.

scoreboard.intro:
The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. On the final code 3b73fe5 against main b455e10, 4 pairs: 0.982 times as fast over the 14 rows, none called better or worse (identical code compared with itself gives about 1.004). JavaScript memory on a reopened long game is +0.0%; geometries grown over 16 moves stay at 10 and textures at 0. Three sections were run again with 8 pairs: the player's own move settled; the rows still over 3% at the median pair are listed under Needs from me.

At the start of the run, main b455e10 against the last run's base 1a04c29 was 1.024 times as fast over the 14 rows, none called. The one lead, the shared game's first screen (7 of 8 pairs slower, not called), follows #155 in a bisect. No comparison calls it, and the same code against itself leans as far (+15%, 7 of 8 pairs), so it stays in the ledger as a measurement question (RG6), with a chart under Not confirmed.

This run did not measure against the first recorded run (92ce041), because no change here was meant to change speed. The last run's figure stands: e02a235 was 2.48 times as fast as 92ce041 over the 11 headline rows both can measure, against a target of 1.2. The chart below is that comparison.

items.title: A record that can't be replayed now says why, once (debc150, fc71549)
items.body: When a game's saved moves could not be replayed, the page showed that the record stopped, and nothing said which move or why. The console now gets a warning with the move and the error, once per failing record: the page replays a frozen record again on every update, and a game against the computer replays it on every check, so the first version repeated itself. The tests that replay a broken record check that it is said once, which also keeps the warning out of the test output.

items.title: Five checks that passed on broken code now fail on it
items.body:
• The notation test for two pieces of different kinds now uses a rook that can actually reach the square, so deleting the kind filter fails it (b861ff5).
  • The rim test now counts every layout read at attach, height and computed style included (4f653b3).
  • The HUD fit test now fails when the turn pill is not measured during a game, where it used to pass without checking (5f36510).
  • A new history test fails if a landing move copies the earlier moves' notation instead of keeping it (006c6d1).
  • A new test fails when a stylesheet reads a custom property, without a fallback, that nothing sets (f0f96ee, c13f805). It found one: --hud-check-ink, read since #73 and never defined.

items.title: Rules that were only written down are now checked
items.body:
• The focus lint (use focusFromCode, not a bare .focus()) now covers the scene and the canvases, which had their own lint blocks without it (119c641).
  • The start page's 12 pictures are checked against the sizes the lens code expects (f1fcd75).
  • bench/loop/.gitignore admits only the files the loop may commit (b6c2991).

items.title: The bench says more
items.body: The review section waits up to 10 s for its button and says what it waited for (3903aaf). A canvas that never came to rest before a timed action is counted and reported (f1e9148). Each join can be traced on demand with BENCH_TRACE_JOIN, and a probe for the shared game's first screen is in bench/loop/tools/join-probe/ (ebef251, 3b73fe5).

removed.intro: Against main, outside bench/loop/, the branch adds 197 lines and removes 84 in 15 files. The app's own code shrinks by 47 lines: −47 in index.css (28 plain sizes that a later rule in the same block always replaced, the play pill's sizes that .lobby-go always overrides, the never-coloured .lobby-error, and a reduced-motion animation: none with no animation left to stop), −2 in ChooseSide.tsx, and +9 for the warning in history.ts, so −40 in all. Tests grow by 117 lines, the bench by 33, and the lint config by 3. The one visible-in-principle deletion, a taller play pill in tall windows, never applied: .lobby-go always won the cascade.

items.title: One component for a move as the move list says it
items.body: It saved no lines, and its first version formatted each move once more per render, which the move list's count test caught. Reverted; in the ledger as 1016-0821:MH1 so it is not retried blind.

rejected.intro: Not tried: a fix for #155's join that keeps its look (builds without the cap unit or text-box moved no wall time in a probe, and no comparison calls a cost), and a faster ambiguity test in the notation (an exploratory timing under node bounds it at about 3% of reopening a long game; parked as 1016-0821:NA1 until an A/B can read that row).

choices.intro:
• The regression check ran against the last run's base (1a04c29), not its bookmark, so that it covered the five PRs main took during the last run.
  • .lobby-error had never been coloured. I deleted the rule rather than make the error red, because red would change what a player sees.
  • The play pill's taller size in tall windows had never applied. I deleted it rather than make it apply.
  • Only the comparisons a decision rests on are committed. Three bisect steps, a cold-load same-code comparison, the probe's traces and timings stay out of git, and the record calls their figures exploratory.
  • The slower join after #155 (RG6) is not put to you: no comparison calls it, and the same code leans as far against itself. It is parked as a question about the bench.
  • The warning is said once per failing record (a WeakSet), so a game against the computer, which replays with no earlier result to compare with, also says it once.
  • Six of the diff reviewers' smaller findings went into the ledger instead of the PR (CF1, CG1, HW1, SV1, AV1, BU1); three were fixed here, and the warning part of HW1 was fixed after grading (fc71549).

notConfirmed.intro:
• That the CSS deletions change nothing on screen rests on reading the cascade and on one-off comparisons of the parsed and computed styles in Chromium, which are not committed. No screenshot pair was made.
  • Whether #155 makes the shared game's first screen slower at all (RG6, chart below). No comparison calls it; the same code leans as far against itself; the probe and the traced bench saw 3–6%.
  • That the capital-sized buttons keep their size in browsers without mod(), round() or the cap unit (Chrome before 125, Safari before 17.2). Read in the source, not loaded in such a browser (ledger CF1).
